newsitem.title: USA: Pollution Research gets flue gas patent.
newsitem.headline: Pollution Research gets flue gas patent.

text.p: Pollution Research and Control Corp said Tuesday it has been awarded a key U.S. patent for its flue gas purification system, adding it will pursue joint ventures and acquisitions to commercialize its proprietary position.

The company said the patent is directed at the air pollution control market for fossil fuel exhaust combustion gases, applications that address a potential worldwide market estimated in excess of $80 billion over the next 10 years.

Pollution Research said the patent provides a proprietary position for removal of oxides of sulfur and nitrogen, ash pollutants and for reducing carbon dioxide levels with steam generator efficiency improvement in the form of direct fuel savings.

In the majority of applications, the realizable annual fuel savings represent a "present value" which may significantly offset the entire capital investment of the pollution control system, chief executive A.E. Gosselin Jr. said.

"This is the first Flue Gas Purification System that yields precise exhaust gas temperature control for efficient pollutant aerosol formation and removal and, in most cases actually save, rather than cost, the user real dollars."

Gosselin continued, "We will pursue two parallel tracks in commercializing the pollution control system -- negotiate a joint venture relationship with an internationally recognized thermal power plant engineering company and/or acquire a power plant engineering company that can be teamed with the fabrication capabilities of our recent acquisition, Nutek Inc, so that we can bid a 'clean-up' system in-house as a sole sub-contractor." -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710
